Quick question from our side ahead of our compliance review next week. When a customer requests account deletion in your hosted offering, can you confirm: 

- The expected window for delete instructions to fully propagate to all backup copies (including offsite replicas) 
- Whether there are any scenarios where a backup copy could be retained beyond the customer-facing delete confirmation (e.g., DR snapshot hold during rolling restore operations)

We need a short, precise statement to include in our internal compliance binder and for the DPO call. A single-paragraph answer is fine; we may follow up for artifacts.

Jack — thanks for the concise ask. Short answer for your binder: 

- Delete propagation window: Redwood initiates deletion immediately upon an authenticated delete request. Metadata-level tombstones are applied in the control plane within minutes; actual removal from primary storage is typically completed within 24 hours.
- Backups / offsite replicas: Backups are subject to configured retention windows. For customers on standard retention, backup snapshots are retained per their account policy (e.g., 30 days) and erased during the next scheduled retention sweep. For accounts that request immediate erasure of backups, Redwood will schedule an expedited erase wave; propagation to all replicas and offsite snapshots is completed within our expedited window of up to 14 days in normal operating conditions.
- DR/restore exceptions: If a live DR operation or in-progress cross-region restore is active at the moment of the delete request, the system will prevent irrecoverable expunge until the DR job finishes; however, expunge is scheduled to run immediately after job completion. These scenarios are limited and tracked — they do not create indefinite retention.

If useful, I can share an exportable one-page statement plus the propagation diagram and the expedited-erase checklist. cc Laura — can you attach the current diagram and playbook?

—Karthik
Director, Product Security & Compliance

- Expedited erase waves are prioritized and include an explicit verification handshake: each replica reports a tombstone + expunge completion event to the control plane; control plane emits a final expunge-confirmation event to the customer's audit log. 
- If an encryption key is scheduled for destruction (customer-managed KMS case), we coordinate key-scheduling with the erase wave; full ciphertext unrecoverability is achieved after key destruction, which is an additional step and may have its own timing constraints. 
- For customers requiring an auditable certificate, we can provide a signed timeline (per-account) showing when each replica reported expunge.
